20. PW 9 Monowar Hossain, Manager, Janata Bank, Nawabpur Branch, Dhaka deposed that on 4-11-1989 the investigating officer seized a cheque bearing No CB-Al 377734 in his presence and prepared seizure list wherein he put his signature which he proved as Exhibits 6 and 6(1) respectively and he identified the seized cheque in the court, which was marked as material Exhibit 1. In cross-examination, he stated that the said cheque was issued in favour of Night Guard Sultan Ahmed. 

 22. PW 14 Liakat Hossain, the Hand Writing Expert, CID Bangladesh, Dhaka, deposed that he examined SB Cheque No. 377734 and letter dated 24-4-1989 and submitted a report which he proved as Exhibit 9 and signature Exhibit 9(1). In cross-examination, he stated that the original page of the cheque and the submitted cheque page were not examined by him. He only examined the disputed signature with the specimen signature of the account holder Shamsul Haque. 

 23. PW 15 Md Azizur Rahman, the Inspector, District Anti-Corruption Bureau, deposed that on 3-9-1989 Md Mushfiqur Rahman, Manager Janata Bank, Shekherchor Bazar Branch made an allegation to the effect that Taka 82,700 was withdrawn from the Savings Account No. 2714 fraudulently. The said allegation was referred to the District Anti-Corruption Officer, Narsingdi who on 30-9-1989 entrusted him to inquire into the allegation. The same was registered as ER No. 49 of 1989 and he inquired the said allegation and on 11-1-1990 he recommended to lodge the case against Md Mushfiqur Rahman, Manager, Md Nurul Amin, Second Officer and AKM Fazlul Haq, Cashier who had fraudulently withdrawn Taka 82,700 and misappropriated the same and committed offence under sections 409,467,471,477A,109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. He submitted all necessary papers of ER No. 49 of 1989, which he proved it as Exhibit 8 and his signature Exhibit 8(1) and inquiry report Exhibit 9 and his signature on it Exhibit 9(1). He further stated that on 15-10-1989 he seized the form of Savings Account No. 2714 which he proved as Exhibit 10. He further stated that on 17-10-1988 Taka 50,000 was withdrawn by Shamsul Haque vide Cheque No. SB/Y 377731 and on 15-11-1988 Taka 9,000 was withdrawn by Shamsul Haque vide Cheque No. SB/Y 377732 and on 3-5-1989 Taka 82,700 was shown to be withdrawn by Shamsul Haq vide Cheque No. SB/AI 377734. On 24-4-1989Abdus Samad was authorised by Shamsul Haque to withdraw Taka 82,700. He further stated that he seized the deposit slip of SB Account No. 2714 and seized one cheque book on 4-1-1989 from the Janata Bank, Nawabpur Branch bearing number SB/ AI 377734 dated 23-2-1989 for Taka 450 (Exhibit-6). In cross-examination he stated that he was not investigating officer of the original case. After preliminary inquiry he recommended for prosecution and subsequently, Md Abdul Mannan Howlader lodged the first information report. He denied the suggestion that without any preliminary inquiry he recommended for prosecution against the accused persons. 

 27. On appraisal and critical analysis of the evidence on record it is evident that PW 12 Md Shamsul Haque opened the Savings Account bearing number 2714 with the Janata Bank, Shekherchor Bazar Branch on depositing cash of Taka 11,000 on 20-4-1987 and up to 13-3-1989 he deposited total Taka 1,43,570 and cheque book was issued in favour of him containing pages bearing No. SB/Y 377731 to SB/Y 377740. It was not disputed that account holder PIN 12 Md Shamsul Haque withdrew Taka 59,000 from his own account by using two pages of the said cheque book and rest eight pages of the cheque book remained intact. It is also not disputed that by cheque No. SB/AI 377740 dated 3-5-1989 one Abdus Samad withdrew Taka 82,700 from the Janata Bank, Shekherchor Branch. It appears that PW 12 account holder Md Shamsul Haque informed that he did not issue any cheque and letter of authority. Then the Manager accused Mushfiqur Rahman referred a letter to the Officer-in-charge of Narsingdi Police Station and it appears from the evidence of PW 15 that on 3-9-1989 Manager Md Mushfiqur by himself made an allegation that Taka 82,700 was fraudulently withdrawn from the Account No. 2714 and the said letter was subsequently referred to the District Anti-Corruption Officer who on 30-9-1989 entrusted him to enquire into the matter. But after inquiry he recommended for prosecution against the accused appellants and another, namely AKM Fazlul Haq, the Cashier of the Bank. It further appears that PW 1 Abdul Mannan Howlader, the informant who was entrusted with the investigation of the case, in his deposition merely proved the First Information Report as Exhibit 1. Moreover, during investigation he seized the cheque book, three pieces of registry slips of application belonging to PW 12 Md Shamsul Haque and prepared seizure list. But those documents were not produced in the court and the same were not proved as evidence. It appears from Material Exhibit 1 that is the cheque bearing No. SB/ Al 377734 dated 3-5-1989 allegedly issued by PW 12 Md Shamsul Haque and the said cheque for Taka 82,700 was disbursed in favour of one Abd us Samad. It appears from the seizure list Exhibit 6 that a cheque bearing No. SB/AI 377734 dated 23-2-1989 for Taka 450 for Janata Bank, Nawabpur Branch, Dhaka issued by account holder Suhan Ahmed was seized. But that cheque was not produced before the court nor the prosecution tried to prove it by evidence. I t further appears that PW 14 Liakat Hossain, a Hand Writing Expert, CID in Dhaka, stated that he examined SB cheque No. 377734 and letter dated 24-4-1989, thereafter he submitted a report Exhibit 9, who on close scrutiny found similarity between the signatures on the specimen signature card of the account holder and signature in the disputed cheque with the letter dated 24-4-1989. So, there is no sufficient and tangible evidence against the appellants to make nexus between them and the alleged offence of breach of trust, forgery of valuable security and criminal misconduct. It further appears to us that the sanction for prosecution of the accused appellants as prescribed in section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 was neither exhibited during trial nor the facts referred to was proved by extraneous evidence, merely in the recital of the charge-sheet.
